headline: Highest risk is data leakage from Chatwoot’s broad network egress into ComfyUI’s vendor-only API path; other pairwise risks are mostly low or none.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can expose customer messages and reports, but ComfyUI has no filesystem read, clipboard, stdin/stdout, or MCP bridge, so a direct injection path is not documented. The only plausible bridge is manual transfer or API-mediated content, which makes hijacking possible but not default. Uncertainty is limited by the profiles, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Chatwoot message content into a ComfyUI prompt or workflow field, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF Chatwoot output is routed through a shared API or queue that ComfyUI parses as instructions, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep Chatwoot outputs out of ComfyUI prompts unless sanitized.
Use a fixed prompt template that treats imported text as data only.
Disable any manual copy-paste workflow between the two systems.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging before any cross-system transfer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while ComfyUI can send data via vendor-only network egress. If Chatwoot content is fed into ComfyUI workflows, sensitive material can leave the local boundary through ComfyUI’s API path. The pairwise interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Chatwoot customer records or messages are passed into ComfyUI inputs, those data may be transmitted to the vendor API.
IF the operator uses shared prompts or workflow text containing customer data, leakage can occur.
mitigations: Do not send customer data into ComfyUI prompts or nodes.
Redact names, emails, order IDs, and message bodies before transfer.
Use a local-only test dataset for any cross-tool workflow.
Review ComfyUI API calls for outbound payload contents.
requires-engineering: add a DLP filter on the handoff path.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress and API integrations, while ComfyUI is single-instance and cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses. There is no documented shared mutable resource or overlapping write surface, so direct capability conflict is limited. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same resource, conflicts can arise.
IF Chatwoot integrations and ComfyUI API calls target the same downstream system, race conditions may appear.
mitigations: Assign separate credentials and destinations to each agent.
Avoid shared writable directories or repos.
Serialize any downstream writes through one controller.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can generate customer-facing content and reports, and ComfyUI can consume API inputs to produce images or workflows. If Chatwoot output is treated as authoritative by ComfyUI-driven automation, errors can cascade into incorrect generated assets or actions. The profiles do not show verification gates, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF ComfyUI workflows consume Chatwoot-generated text without validation, downstream outputs may reflect Chatwoot errors.
IF generated images or workflow artifacts are used operationally, a mistaken Chatwoot input can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before ComfyUI consumes Chatwoot output.
Use schema validation on any transferred fields.
Limit the transfer to non-authoritative metadata.
Log source-to-destination mappings for each handoff.
requires-engineering: add automated verification between systems.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and messages, while ComfyUI is a vendor-facing image-generation system with vendor-only egress. If regulated customer or EU personal data is moved from Chatwoot into ComfyUI, residency and retention obligations may diverge. The profiles do not specify certifications or DPA coverage, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF EU personal data from Chatwoot is sent into ComfyUI, residency or transfer obligations may be triggered.
IF customer messages contain regulated data and are retained in ComfyUI logs or outputs, retention mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of ComfyUI inputs.
Use synthetic or anonymized examples for image generation.
Check retention settings on both systems before sharing data.
Document the lawful basis and transfer path for any cross-system data.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class.
